speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are experiencing a psychiatric condition alongside a new onset movement disorder; could you please describe the specific movements you are noticing?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that history. Risperidone is a common cause of new movement disorders; could you describe the specific movements you are noticing in detail, such as stiffness, tremors, or rhythmic jerking?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inability to remain still, persistent feeling of restlessness. I also have Frequent fidgeting, Repetitive crossing and uncrossing of legs, Pacing.

speaker: Doctor
text: The symptoms you describe—restlessness, fidgeting, and leg crossing—are classic signs of akathisia, a known side effect of risperidone. Have you noticed any worsening of this feeling or any muscle stiffness since starting the medication two months ago?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Recently diagnosed with schizophrenia. No other significant past medical history. Social history: College student, lives with parents. Denies tobacco, alcohol, or drug use.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Akathisia secondary to risperidone use.
